WITH race_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    r.name,
    AVG(ds.points) as avg_points,
    COUNT(*) as count_records
  FROM driverStandings ds
  JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
overall_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(count_records) as overall_avg_count
  FROM race_stats
),
filtered_races AS (
  SELECT 
    rs.avg_points,
    rs.count_records,
    os.overall_avg_count
  FROM race_stats rs
  CROSS JOIN overall_stats os
  WHERE rs.count_records > os.overall_avg_count
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_points) as avg_of_avg_points,
  AVG(count_records) as avg_of_counts,
  AVG(count_records - overall_avg_count) as avg_of_excess
FROM filtered_races

assumptions.assumption: Race names can repeat across different races (e.g., 'Monaco Grand Prix' appears in multiple years), and all driverStandings records with the same race name are aggregated together for the per-name statistics. This is consistent with F1 historical data.
